messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE employee (
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    City TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE shop (
    Shop_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Location TEXT,
    District TEXT,
    Number_products INT,
    Manager_name TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE hiring (
    Shop_ID INT,
    Employee_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Start_from TEXT,
    Is_full_time bool,
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Shop_ID) REFERENCES shop(Shop_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE evaluation (
    Employee_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Year_awarded TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Bonus REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    UNIQUE (Employee_ID, Year_awarded),
    FOREIGN KEY (Employee_ID) REFERENCES employee(Employee_ID)
);

```sql
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```

If you mean only “stores with *many* products” above a threshold, tell me the minimum number (e.g., `>= 100`), or use:

```sql
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products >= 100
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```
many products means more than the average for all stores

```sql
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > (SELECT AVG(Number_products) FROM shop)
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```
you might want to look at stores that have a higher count than a certain threshold.

```sql
-- replace :threshold with your number (e.g., 100)
SELECT
  Shop_ID,
  Name,
  Location,
  District,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > :threshold
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```
also, we should just focus on getting the names of the stores that meet the criteria.

```sql
-- Stores with products above the overall average
SELECT Name
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > (SELECT AVG(Number_products) FROM shop)
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```

```sql
-- Stores with products above a chosen threshold (replace :threshold)
SELECT Name
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > :threshold
ORDER BY Number_products DESC;
```
We should also keep track of how many products each store has.

```sql
-- Above-average stores, keeping product counts
SELECT
  Name,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > (SELECT AVG(Number_products) FROM shop)
ORDER BY Number_products DESC, Name;
```

```sql
-- Threshold-based, keeping product counts (replace :threshold)
SELECT
  Name,
  Number_products
FROM shop
WHERE Number_products > :threshold
ORDER BY Number_products DESC, Name;
```
